text:
alicia: Heads up — after the model-serving rollout in us-west2 we're seeing a huge cardinality spike into Cortex and remote_write 504s. p95 write latency to remote cluster jumped. :eyes:

mike: saw it too, grafana alert fired for remote_write_error_rate. charts show a sudden bump in unique series from gpu-exporter pods.

jin: any recent config changes to relabeling? sounds like a label leak.

alicia: we rolled a change that adds per-job labels for batch training. I thought we were only annotating pods, not exporter metrics. could be leaking job_id into metrics.

infra-eng: confirmed. `kubectl get pods -l app=gpu-exporter -n infra -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.labels}'` shows `training-job=job-{{id}}` on a subset of nodes. exporter picks that up as a label -> explosion.

mike: that explains series count. ops-lead can we throttle/disable scrapes for those nodes while we patch?

ops-lead: yes, we can push a quick relabel to drop training-job at scrape time. adding to prometheus scrape_configs for gpu-exporter: 

```
# temporary fix
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_training-job]
    action: drop
    regex: .+
```

mike: careful — our metadata key is `training-job` but the meta label is `__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_training_job` (underscore vs hyphen). the current snippet won't match.

jin: oh nice catch. correct snippet: 
```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_training_job]
    action: drop
    regex: .+
```

alicia: Pushed a hotfix to staging prometheus, will roll to prod in 5. also opened a ticket to patch the code path that annotates pods.

sre-bot: alert: remote_write_5xx_rate > 5% in us-west2 (details: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/remote-write)

infra-eng: short term: we also reduced scrape_interval from 15s to 60s for gpu-exporter on affected nodes and set `scrape_timeout: 10s` to avoid hanging requests. that immediately reduced queue pressure on the remote_write path.

mike: any idea why remote_write started 504ing instead of buffering? we've hit high cardinality before and it buffered.

ops-lead: remote cluster egress was at ~95% of bandwidth due to background model syncs (same nodes). combined with bigger payloads (more series) caused proxied requests to time out instead of being retried.

jin: for long term: we should add a `metric_relabel_configs` to the scrape job to explicitly drop `training_job`, `epoch`, `run_id`, and any label matching `job-.*` so rogue annotations don't explode cardinality. also add a test in CI that simulates exporters with dynamic labels.

alicia: agreed. i'll add the metric_relabel_configs + a prometheus rule to alarm when unique_series_rate > 2x baseline.

ops-lead: cost note — these spikes triple our ingestion egress and Cortex storage write patterns. infra to estimate cost delta for Q2 if we let this pattern continue.

infra-eng: I'll run a quick query for bytes_out by cluster over last 6h and share in #incidents.

mike: thanks. for now, confirm the prod relabel is applied?

alicia: prod relabel rolled. series creation rate back down to normal. remote_write 5xx rate trending to 0. keeping watch for 30m.

jin: followups:
- revert pod-annotation change from model deploys until we vet it
- add CI test + metric_relabel_configs to gpu-exporter job
- cost impact assessment (infra)
- add a runbook snippet on how to quickly reduce scrape_frequency for a node pool

ops-lead: created incident-206543 in ops tracker and assigned followups.

mike: great job catching the mismatch quickly. :thumbsup:
